name: Pop screen print
summary: A photograph or a found image pulled through a silk screen in flat, bright inks, often with the black photo layer off register. Warhol made it a studio process in 1962; Corita Kent printed text and colour; the look stands for pop art.

philosophy.core_thesis: A mechanical image, repeated and coloured by hand in loud inks, makes the familiar new.
design_principles: Start from a found photograph, cut to high contrast or a coarse halftone, in a black ink.
Put 2–5 flat, opaque, bright colours under the black, cut by hand and a little loose from the photo.
Let the black layer miss the colour by 2–5 mm, so the hand shows.
Repeat the same image in a grid with different colour sets.
Use colours from advertising: hot pink, lemon, turquoise, orange.
Keep the ink films thick and the edges a little uneven where the squeegee dragged.
anti_patterns: A soft photographic tone with no contrast
Exact register that hides the process
A painterly brush texture over the whole sheet

process.matrix: A silk or nylon mesh on a wood frame, with a photo stencil for the image and cut stencils for the colours.
process.press: A flat bed with a hinged frame and a rubber squeegee, pulled by hand.
process.image_making: The artist picks the photo and the colours; studio assistants burn the screens and pull the prints.
process.edition: A portfolio of 10 prints in 250 copies, or unique canvases.

inks.strategy: Thick, opaque screen inks: flat colour areas first, the black photo layer last.

colours.name: Turquoise
colours.role: the eye shadow and the ground

screening.rule: Use a coarse halftone of 20–40 lines an inch for the photo layer, or cut it to pure black and white.

registration.rule: The photo layer can sit 2–5 mm off the colour; the shift is a feature.

substrate.stock: A heavy wove paper (Beckett, Arches) or primed canvas.
substrate.finish: Smooth, bright white or cream, uncoated.

surface.impression: No bite; the thick ink stands on the surface.
surface.sheen: A satin film with a slight gloss in the dark inks.
surface.texture: Flat, dense colour with a squeegee drag at the edges and a coarse dot in the photo.

marks: repeated grid of the same image

evidence.title: The Drunkard poster
evidence.maker: Federal Theatre Project, Works Progress Administration

evidence.title: Emperor Jones Poster 1937
evidence.maker: Federal Theatre Project, Works Progress Administration

emotion.target_response: Glamour with a wink: the viewer sees fame and consumer goods made loud and ironic.

avoid_when: The subject needs a sober or a respectful treatment.
The photo has too little contrast to cut.

modifiers.how: Use a fixed dot tint on the colours and a firm black line, as in a comic.
Photocopy the photo in black on white paper and paste the text on by hand.
Print 2–3 transparent riso inks with a grain screen; let them mix where they overlap.

sources.title: Frayda Feldman and Jörg Schellmann, Andy Warhol Prints: A Catalogue Raisonné (D.A.P., 2003)
